experiment.name: prompt-tuning-classifier
experiment.question: Does a cross-source prompt outperform the baseline classifier on a B2B SaaS transaction-categorization task?
experiment.metric: Classification accuracy vs human-labeled ground truth (judge: Claude Sonnet 4.6)
experiment.threshold_rule: Aggregate effect >= +5pp AND no per-slice loss > 2pp (CI lower bound) AND no per-failure-mode regression in the highest-severity category (transfer_as_revenue)

verdict.rationale: v2 passes all three pre-registered rules: (a) aggregate effect +8.9pp, CI lower bound +5.0pp == threshold; (b) per-slice — Enterprise +13.4pp, SMB +6.7pp, both CI lower bounds positive; (c) per-failure-mode — `transfer_as_revenue` drops from 4 to 2, and severity-weighted accuracy rises from 0.581 to 0.724. v3 ties v2 on aggregate (+8.9pp) but FAILS two of three rules: SMB per-slice -3.3pp with CI [-8.8pp, +2.2pp] crossing the -2pp loss floor, AND `transfer_as_revenue` failures rise from 4 to 6 (the highest-severity category, weight 3.0). The severity-weighted score confirms it: v3 = 0.572 is BELOW baseline 0.581 despite tying v2 on unweighted aggregate. Aggregate winners that lose on a major slice or shift errors into the highest-severity category are not winners. Ship v2; kill v3.
